text: {"observations":"Clear vocal harmonic stacks with pitch glides and vibrato (e.g. 0.7-1.2 s, 3.6-4.6 s, around 5 s) plus sibilant noise bursts up to 7 kHz show a single lead singer over steady instrumental tones, ruling out D (instrumental) and making C (choir) unlikely since there is one harmonic series rather than several blended ones. Harmonic spacing in the zoom is about 230-280 Hz, so the fundamental sits around B3-D4. That pitch is ambiguous, but the harmonics stay strong and dense up to 6-7 kHz, which fits a male voice pushed into its upper range better than a female voice low in its range. I lean A over B, with moderate confidence.","answer":"A"}
